items.title: Document leak at Australia's richest company shows how it put off going green
items.description: Hundreds of pages of internal BHP documents reveal how the company sold itself as a climate leader while internally finding reasons to put off action in the Pilbara.

items.title: Trump demands Arab nations recognise Israel as part of Iran war deal
items.description: Donald Trump has boldly tied negotiations to end his war with Iran to a swathe of Arab nations formally establishing diplomatic ties with Israel.

items.title: Iran says 'no tolls' on Strait of Hormuz, but warns everything has a cost
items.description: While on assignment inside Iran, our reporter asked a foreign ministry official about the regime's plan for the Strait of Hormuz. The spokesperson responded that "there is no toll" but also signalled crossing the strait will not be entirely free.

items.title: 'Fool, ignoramus': Parliamentary committee suspended as senators clash
items.description: A heated exchange prompted a Liberal senator to step in and call point of order on the Labor chair after several insults directed at Nationals senator Bridget McKenzie, before a brief suspension.

items.title: Labor calls for spare change as One Nation surges
items.description: Federal Labor is asking for donations to fight One Nation as the latest polling shows the minor party continuing to surge in key electorates, including in Western Sydney.

items.title: Australian astronaut offered place on breakthrough space flight
items.description: The European Space Agency has formally extended the offer for Australia's Katherine Bennell-Pegg to join a mission that would take her to the International Space Station, but the place is not guaranteed.

items.title: More than 20 hospitalised after substance sprayed in Tokyo mall
items.description: The shopping centre, located in the touristy and upmarket shopping district of Ginza, has been blocked off following the incident.

items.title: Renewables company destroys Indigenous shelter despite knowing about it
items.description: ACREZ apologises to traditional owners "without reservation" as the NSW Environment Minister Penny Sharpe expresses her "fury" at the incident.

items.title: ASIO reviewed past terror cases in 2024 but didn't re-examine Bondi attackers
items.description: The head of Australia's domestic intelligence agency reveals it reviewed past terrorism investigations in 2024 which did not extend to a re-examination of the soon to be Bondi gunmen because of a resourcing decision.

items.title: Crews to work overnight after burst pipe in Melbourne leaves thousands without power
items.description: A power company was forced to switch off power to about 10,000 customers in the heart of Melbourne after a burst water main threatened to flood a substation on Monday afternoon.

items.title: 'I did it': Parramatta council official fronts corruption watchdog
items.description: During her third day on the witness stand, Roxanne Thornton told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) she was responsible for hiring processes that were "extremely flawed".

items.title: Neale Daniher, former AFL player and motor neurone disease campaigner, dies aged 65
items.description: Former Essendon player and Demons coach Neale Daniher has died, aged 65. He was diagnosed with motor neurone disease in 2013 and campaigned to raise awareness of the disease and increase research.

items.title: Dezi Freeman goaded officers to 'come and get me' before fatal shooting
items.description: The Coroners Court has heard about Dezi Freeman's final moments before a fatal confrontation at his hideout in Victoria's north-east.

items.title: V'landys to take over as NRL CEO after Abdo quits to join Tennis Australia
items.description: NRL CEO Andrew Abdo causes a shock in the rugby league world by departing mid-season after a highly-successful six-year stint.

items.title: These mince recipes require minimal effort for maximum flavour
items.description: Mix up your mince menu with these versatile and affordable meals for the whole family.

items.title: Death of 'drongo': Are Aussie insults and swearwords dying out?
items.description: Classic Australian swearwords and insults are becoming less popular with younger generations. What does losing them mean for our culture?

items.title: A movie about mystery-hunting sheep delights this May
items.description: Plus the rom-com of yore returns in Finding Emily, the farmyard mystery that's been delighting audiences, and a gory Hollywood video game adaptation filmed on the Gold Coast.

items.title: Magnussen flops at Enhanced Games, finishes last twice
items.description: James Magnussen, wearing a garish golden suit, has finished dead last at the inaugural Enhanced Games event.

items.title: Man found not guilty of murdering Darwin mother a 'serious risk' to community
items.description: Sheena Fairfield was brutally stabbed to death in the yard of her suburban home in 2022. The man charged with her murder never went to trial due to mental impairment but he could be detained for 20 years.

items.title: Man, 23, charged with murder over death of eight-week-old baby
items.description: A 23-year-old man has been charged with murder over the death of an eight-week-old child in suburban Perth.

items.title: Man jailed for fatally amputating man's foot using circular saw
items.description: Kalman Tal's loved ones have told of their distress at how the 66-year-old's leg was amputated in a public park. Farm worker John Yalu has today been sentenced for manslaughter.

items.title: Blues send out SOS as playmaker struggles with injury
items.description: A hamstring complaint for Mitchell Moses puts a scare through the NSW Blues, with Ethan Strange stepping up and Matt Burton called into camp ahead of State of Origin I.

items.title: Dog-friendly cafe issued warning after customer complaint
items.description: Kellie Hunter opened her cafe in the Adelaide Hills in 2023 as a friendly place for dogs and their owners, but the local council has now put a stop to it after one complaint.

items.title: ISIS-linked women and children to return to Australia within days
items.description: A group of women and children linked to Islamic State fighters are expected to arrive home within days after purchasing flights to Australia.

items.title: NACC boss Paul Brereton resigns amid pressure over misconduct, defence ties
items.description: Mr Brereton was found in 2024 to have engaged in officer misconduct in his role as head of the NACC and has since faced pressure over his defence connections.
